_comment: Black Box rule-engine config. Edit this file to add/disable/tune rules without touching main.js. Restart the app after editing. NOT machine learning — every rule here is a simple, explicit heuristic, and is labeled as such in the UI and exported fault packages.

name_based_rules.label: Possible Cavitation (rule-based)
name_based_rules._note: Fires only if signal names containing all three substrings are present in the same captured event. Works only when channels are named descriptively.

name_based_rules.label: Possible Overheat (rule-based)
name_based_rules._note: Fires if any captured signal name contains 'temp'.

name_based_rules.label: Possible Pressure Anomaly (rule-based)
name_based_rules._note: Broader than cavitation — fires on 'pressure' alone, without requiring flow/current too.

name_based_rules.label: Possible Slave Unreachable (rule-based)
name_based_rules._note: MBTCP diagnostic rule. Intended use: pair with ActiveConnection=0 in the captured window for a real diagnosis — today this only checks the FailedConnection name is present in the event, not the ActiveConnection value. Treat as a starting tag, not a confirmed root cause.

name_based_rules.label: Possible Protocol/Register Mismatch (rule-based)
name_based_rules._note: Modbus exception 0x01 (Illegal Function) reported by the slave.

name_based_rules.label: Possible Protocol/Register Mismatch — Illegal Address (rule-based)
name_based_rules._note: Modbus exception 0x02 (Illegal Data Address) — commonly a wrong register address configured on the master.

name_based_rules.label: Possible Slave Overload/Timeout (rule-based)
name_based_rules._note: Intended use: pair with ResponsePerSecond flat/falling in the captured window — today only checks RequestLossPerSecond's name is present, not its trend.

name_based_rules.label: Slave Device Fault — directly reported, not inferred (rule-based)
name_based_rules._note: Modbus exception 0x04 — the slave itself is reporting an internal fault. This is the one rule that is not a heuristic: if this signal is present and nonzero in the event, the device said so directly.

value_based_rules.label: Signal Flatlined (rule-based)
value_based_rules._note: Fires if a signal's value does not change at all for at least min_seconds within the captured window. Works regardless of signal naming — useful for generic/unnamed registers. Logic not yet implemented in main.js; schema only for now.

value_based_rules.label: Sudden Spike/Drop (rule-based)
value_based_rules._note: Fires if a sample-to-sample change exceeds factor x the signal's recent average step size within the captured window. Works regardless of naming. Logic not yet implemented in main.js; schema only for now.

_relationship_rules_note: Intentionally empty. Comparing two channels against each other (e.g. 'Channel A should track Channel B within X%') depends entirely on how the user commissions/wires their MBTCP devices — it cannot be guessed from signal names or values alone. This needs an explicit user-defined pairing (e.g. a future config UI or a relationship_rules.json), not a built-in heuristic. Treat as a Phase 2 item.
